input.prompt: Is there any maximum request body size limit (e.g., MAXIMUM_MESSAGE_SIZE, maxBodySize, 4mb, content-length check, 413)? Quote relevant lines exactly.

toolu_01JUki9HdPeq1ucQpMff2taL.prompt: Is there any maximum request body size limit (e.g., MAXIMUM_MESSAGE_SIZE, maxBodySize, 4mb, content-length check, 413)? Quote relevant lines exactly.

content.content:
**Yes.** The transport limits POST body size, using the option `maxRequestBodySize`. The name `MAXIMUM_MESSAGE_SIZE` does not appear in the source.

The option is documented as:

> "Upper bound, in bytes, on a POST body the transport reads itself."

> "@default 4194304 (4 MiB)"

> "Not applied when the caller supplies `parsedBody`."

The constructor resolves the limit:

> "this._maxRequestBodySize = resolveMaxRequestBodySize(options.maxRequestBodySize);"

When the body is read, the limit is enforced:

> "const body = await readRequestBody(req, this._maxRequestBodySize);"

> "if (body.tooLarge) {"

> "return this.createJsonErrorResponse(413, -32000, message);"

The 413 status is the only size-related response shown. The body-reading helper `readRequestBody` is not included in the content, so I can't confirm the exact `Content-Length` and streaming checks from the code itself. The option's doc comment describes them, though.

Separately, `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` limits the number of messages in a batch, not bytes. The check is `rawMessage.length > MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, which returns a 400 error. The value of `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is not shown.

content.text:
By default, the largest request body it accepts is **4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes)**. You can change that limit.

In the current `v1.x` branch, the limit comes from the `maxRequestBodySize` option on the Streamable HTTP server transport (`WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport`, which the Node `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` wraps):

- **Default:** the option's doc comment says "Upper bound, in bytes, on a POST body the transport reads itself … @default 4194304 (4 MiB)".
- **If the body is too big:** the server replies with HTTP **413** and JSON-RPC error code `-32000`.
- **Changing it:** pass `maxRequestBodySize` in the transport options.
- **Exception:** the limit doesn't apply if you pass a pre-parsed body (`parsedBody`), for example from Express `body-parser`. In that case your middleware's limit is the one that counts. Express's `express.json()` defaults to 100 KB.
- **Batches:** there is also a separate `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` that caps how many messages a JSON-RPC batch can hold. Too many returns HTTP 400. This is a message count, not a byte size, and I didn't confirm its value.

Older releases hard-coded `MAXIMUM_MESSAGE_SIZE = "4mb"` and enforced it with `raw-body`, so the number has stayed 4 MB. The newer option just makes it adjustable.

I checked Ludion first and it had nothing on this. The answer above comes from the SDK's `v1.x` source. The `main` branch has been split into separate packages and I didn't check it, so look there too if you're on the v2 packages.

Sources:
- [typescript-sdk v1.x `webStandardStreamableHttp.ts`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/v1.x/src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts)
- [typescript-sdk v1.x `streamableHttp.ts`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/v1.x/src/server/streamableHttp.ts)
- [Older snapshot showing `MAXIMUM_MESSAGE_SIZE = "4mb"` (glama.ai mirror)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/@Jeffwalters9597/MCP/blob/0506addf35f422650658c5e665ea184e3115a184/src/server/streamableHttp.ts)
